Has Bitcoin Replaced Gold As The New Safe Haven?

Don't think so.

In the face of the recent price action in gold and the relative calm in BTC it might be tempting to think people are accumulating BTC where they would have bought gold. I think this is too simple.

China was expected to be a large buyer of gold for years. The economy was booming, and the PBOC was expected to be holding more gold than they had announced publicly. When their revisions came out, it was more than claimed but lower than expectations, and China's market is tanking. At the same time, the US claims they're going to raise rates. Gold is a great hedge against inflation and a desireable store of value to the Chinese. The outlook for demand on both fronts has changed.

So what about BTC? We experienced a bubble. The price shot up to 1200, fell to 200, and corrected. We're still discovering the price after over a year of overvaluation. It remains an incredible unknown. SHA 256 is not a safe haven to people like me who don't know enough to know if there's a serious vulnerability. How well positioned am I to feel reasonably secure? Better than most. So for whom is BTC a safe haven? cryptography experts maybe, but maybe even some of them think Bitcoin's cryptography will be cracked like so many earlier forms of digital security.

BTC I think is still a speculative but very powerful currency. It's valuation depends largely on what it can do and how quickly it can do it. It is not a safe haven in the way gold is a safe haven. If it were perhaps it would be sliding to the extent that gold slides as a hedge against inflation.

SHA 256 is not a safe haven to people like me who don't know enough to know if there's a serious vulnerability. How well positioned am I to feel reasonably secure? Better than most. So for whom is BTC a safe haven? cryptography experts maybe, but maybe even some of them think Bitcoin's cryptography will be cracked like so many earlier forms of digital security.

So it's time you found out enough of 'what you don't know' then. You don't know or understand the security system of your bank, yet you leave your valuables there. Why? It's simply that enough people you trust told you it's safe, and what they said made sense to you. With bitcoin it's all new, so there are fewer people around to give you that warm fuzzy feeling, yet you need to find it eventually.
BTC is still far to small to compare - we are talking about 0,1% of gold market by capitalisation.
